newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Tax dampens Spain's Tabacalera.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Tax dampens Spain's Tabacalera.

text.p: Spanish tobacco group Tabacalera posted a 4.7 percent rise in nine-month pretax profit on Monday, but the figures were received cautiously because of a recent hike in special taxes on tobacco, analysts said.
Tabacalera said group pretax profit rose to 14.38 billion pesetas ($113.4 million) on a 7.1 percent increase in net turnover.
But sales net of taxes and commissions, hit by a government tax increase on tobacco in July, fell 6.3 percent to 238.58 billion pesetas.

"At the parent level, gross profit fell seven percent, although at the group it rose 4.7 percent due to non-specified extraordinary income. And while the company doesn't quantify the amount, it's difficult to make an exact valuation on how business is going," said an analyst at a Madrid brokerage.
The company simply said the divestment of stakes in sugar firm Ebro and olive oil producer Koipe and related adjustments -- mainly goodwill depreciation -- generated extraordinary gains.
A spokesman for the firm said net attributable profit for the nine months to September was 10.44 billion pesetas, versus 9.28 billion in the year-earlier period.
Analysts did not expect the company to realise capital gains in the third quarter, and had forecast on average a 10 percent fall in net profit to 8.39 billion pesetas.

The forecasts stemmed from an anticipated slump in operating margin after the government's increase of alcohol and tobacco taxes, and the firm's decision not to tack the hike onto cigarettes of internationally competitive Virginia tobacco.
Tabacalera said this decision had slowed down the increase in income from tobacco sales.
The firm's financial director Calixto Rios told Reuters Financial Television that any move to pass the tax hike to retail cigarette prices would hinge on what its competitors did.
"We are watching carefully the market situation and we will move accordingly," he said.
The sale of the government's 52 percent stake in Tabacalera seems likely to take place sometime towards the end of 1997 or at the start of 1998, he added.
The capital gains realised on the sale of the Ebro and Koipe stakes and the adjustments made to goodwill depreciation could amount to around 600 million pesetas, according to one analyst.
Although analysts highlighted the need for a further breakdown of figures from the company, they pointed out that the results were much better than the more pessimistic forecasts had indicated.
Some had been expecting up to a 20 percent fall in profit after the tax hike. ($1=126.8 Peseta)
